raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Since #42175, `Qwen4ExpLayerExtensionMixin` imports `sglang.srt.layers.moe.qwen4_decode` unconditionally. That module imports `custom_all_reduce_v2`, which imports `tvm_ffi`. The XPU install (`pyproject_xpu.toml`) does not provide `tvm_ffi`, so Qwen4Exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) models fail during layer construction on Intel GPUs:

```
File ".../sglang/srt/layers/moe/qwen4_decode.py", line 15, in <module>
    from sglang.srt.distributed.device_communicators.custom_all_reduce_v2 import (
File ".../sglang/srt/distributed/device_communicators/custom_all_reduce_v2.py", line 35, in <module>
    from sglang.kernels.ops.communication.all_reduce import (
File ".../sglang/kernels/ops/communication/all_reduce.py", line 7, in <module>
    import tvm_ffi
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tvm_ffi'
```

`prepare_qwen4_decode_comm` already returns `None` unless the device is CUDA SM10, so the import is not needed on other platforms.

Enabling the existing qwen4 tests on XPU (as asked in review) also showed that the PLE prefetch stream was a `torch.cuda.Stream`, so a Qwen4Exp model with `ple_offload_embedding` could not be built on XPU either.

## Modifications

1. `[Fix] [Intel] qwen4_exp: only import qwen4_decode on CUDA`: a small helper, `_prepare_decode_moe_comm(mlp)`, imports `qwen4_decode` and calls `prepare_qwen4_decode_comm` only on CUDA for a `Qwen2MoeSparseMoeBlock`; otherwise `None`, which is what the non-CUDA path got before. The second import in `_run_ffn_stage` is only reached when `_decode_moe_comm` is not `None`, so it needs no change. New `test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen4_exp_decode_comm.py` (CPU and XPU CI) fails any import of `qwen4_decode` and checks that a MoE layer off CUDA, and a dense layer anywhere, never import it.
2. `[Intel] qwen4_exp: device-agnostic PLE prefetch stream; run the PLE offload test on XPU`: the four PLE prefetch-stream calls use `torch.get_device_module()` (the `torch.cuda` module on CUDA, so CUDA is unchanged). `test/registered/kernels/ops/embeddings/test_qwen4_ple_offload.py` takes its device from `torch.accelerator` (CUDA or XPU), uses `torch.accelerator` memory stats, and is registered with `register_xpu_ci(est_time=45, suite="stage-b-test-1-gpu-xpu")`. The file-backend cases stay CUDA-only (they check host page-table access through the CUDA runtime) and skip on XPU as before.

## Accuracy Tests

No change to model outputs on CUDA: the CUDA branch of the helper runs the same calls as before, and `torch.get_device_module()` is `torch.cuda` there.

On 1x Intel Arc Pro B70 (torch 2.14.0+xpu, sglang-kernel-xpu 0.4.0, this branch on main fdc2dd0d05):

```
pytest test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen4_exp_decode_comm.py \
       test/registered/kernels/ops/embeddings/test_qwen4_ple_offload.py \
       test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen4_exp_ple_table.py \
       test/registered/unit/layer_boundary/test_qwen4_exp_ple_rows.py
32 passed, 6 skipped
```

The 6 skips are the existing CUDA-only checks (file backend, pinned memory through the CUDA runtime). Before the stream change, `test_qwen4_ple_offload_avoids_device_table` failed on XPU with `RuntimeError: torch.cuda.Stream requires CUDA support` (`qwen4_exp.py:1109`). With `_is_cuda` forced on and a MoE block, the new test's import guard does catch the `qwen4_decode` import, so it would catch a regression.

End to end, 4-layer dummy-weight Qwen3.8-Flash-Next config (`--load-format dummy --device xpu --attention-backend intel_xpu`), same card: main fdc2dd0d05 fails at model construction with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tvm_ffi'`; this branch starts and serves eager decode at C1/C2/C4 (512-token random prompts, 256 new tokens).

Not run: CUDA (no NVIDIA GPU here; CUDA behaviour is unchanged by construction, and CI will cover it).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not performance-related.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

nodes.body:
Still applies on current main: `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen4_exp.py:1593` imports `qwen4_decode` unconditionally, so Qwen4Exp construction still fails on XPU installs without `tvm_ffi`. The branch merges cleanly (259 commits behind, no conflicts in the one touched file).

The red checks are only `pr-gate` (missing the `run-ci` label). @BBuf (author of #42175) or @arathi-hlab, could one of you take a look and add `run-ci` if it looks right? Thanks.

@airMeng done, thanks for picking this up. Rebased on main (fdc2dd0d05), two commits:

1. The `qwen4_decode` gate, now in a small helper `_prepare_decode_moe_comm`, plus a unit test (`test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen4_exp_decode_comm.py`, CPU and XPU CI) that fails any import of `qwen4_decode` off CUDA.
2. `test/registered/kernels/ops/embeddings/test_qwen4_ple_offload.py` now runs on XPU and is registered for `stage-b-test-1-gpu-xpu`. Enabling it found one more XPU blocker: the PLE prefetch stream was a `torch.cuda.Stream` (`RuntimeError: torch.cuda.Stream requires CUDA support` when building a model with `ple_offload_embedding`), so those four calls now use `torch.get_device_module()`. That is still `torch.cuda` on CUDA.

On one Arc Pro B70 (torch 2.14.0+xpu, sglang-kernel-xpu 0.4.0), the four qwen4 test files give 32 passed and 6 skipped. The skips are the existing CUDA-only file-backend and pinned-memory checks. The e2e dummy Flash-Next server fails on main with the `tvm_ffi` error and serves on this branch. Details are in the description. The two e2e tests (`test_qwen4_exp_models.py`, the PD prefill CP test) need multi-GPU B200 setups, so I left their registration alone. Happy to split commit 2 out if you'd rather keep the bundle smaller.

+"""Qwen4-exp layers import the CUDA-only qwen4_decode module on CUDA only.
+
+qwen4_decode pulls in custom_all_reduce_v2, which needs tvm_ffi; the XPU and
+CPU installs do not ship it, so importing it there failed layer construction.
+"""
+
+import sys
+import unittest
+from unittest import mock
+
+from sglang.srt.models import qwen4_exp as qwen4_exp_module
+from sglang.srt.models.qwen2_moe import Qwen2MoeSparseMoeBlock
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci, register_xpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+register_xpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="stage-b-test-1-gpu-xpu")
+
+_DECODE_MODULE = "sglang.srt.layers.moe.qwen4_decode"
+
+
+class _BlockDecodeImport:
+    """A meta path finder that fails any import of qwen4_decode."""
+
+    def find_spec(self, name, path=None, target=None):
+        if name == _DECODE_MODULE:
+            raise AssertionError(f"{_DECODE_MODULE} imported off CUDA")
+        return None
+
+
+class TestQwen4ExpDecodeComm(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        sys.modules.pop(_DECODE_MODULE, None)
+        finder = _BlockDecodeImport()
+        sys.meta_path.insert(0, finder)
+        self.addCleanup(sys.meta_path.remove, finder)
+
+    def test_moe_layer_off_cuda_skips_qwen4_decode(self):
+        mlp = Qwen2MoeSparseMoeBlock.__new__(Qwen2MoeSparseMoeBlock)
+        with mock.patch.object(qwen4_exp_module, "_is_cuda", False):
+            self.assertIsNone(qwen4_exp_module._prepare_decode_moe_comm(mlp))
+        self.assertNotIn(_DECODE_MODULE, sys.modules)
+
+    def test_dense_layer_skips_qwen4_decode(self):
+        with mock.patch.object(qwen4_exp_module, "_is_cuda", True):
+            self.assertIsNone(qwen4_exp_module._prepare_decode_moe_comm(object()))
+        self.assertNotIn(_DECODE_MODULE, sys.modules)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

Still applies on current main: `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen4_exp.py:1593` imports `qwen4_decode` unconditionally, so Qwen4Exp construction still fails on XPU installs without `tvm_ffi`. The branch merges cleanly (259 commits behind, no conflicts in the one touched file).

The red checks are only `pr-gate` (missing the `run-ci` label). @BBuf (author of #42175) or @arathi-hlab, could one of you take a look and add `run-ci` if it looks right? Thanks.

@airMeng done, thanks for picking this up. Rebased on main (fdc2dd0d05), two commits:

1. The `qwen4_decode` gate, now in a small helper `_prepare_decode_moe_comm`, plus a unit test (`test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen4_exp_decode_comm.py`, CPU and XPU CI) that fails any import of `qwen4_decode` off CUDA.
2. `test/registered/kernels/ops/embeddings/test_qwen4_ple_offload.py` now runs on XPU and is registered for `stage-b-test-1-gpu-xpu`. Enabling it found one more XPU blocker: the PLE prefetch stream was a `torch.cuda.Stream` (`RuntimeError: torch.cuda.Stream requires CUDA support` when building a model with `ple_offload_embedding`), so those four calls now use `torch.get_device_module()`. That is still `torch.cuda` on CUDA.

On one Arc Pro B70 (torch 2.14.0+xpu, sglang-kernel-xpu 0.4.0), the four qwen4 test files give 32 passed and 6 skipped. The skips are the existing CUDA-only file-backend and pinned-memory checks. The e2e dummy Flash-Next server fails on main with the `tvm_ffi` error and serves on this branch. Details are in the description. The two e2e tests (`test_qwen4_exp_models.py`, the PD prefill CP test) need multi-GPU B200 setups, so I left their registration alone. Happy to split commit 2 out if you'd rather keep the bundle smaller.
